newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Senate urges East Timorese self-rule.
newsitem.headline: Australian Senate urges East Timorese self-rule.

text.p: The Australian Senate on Wednesday called for self-determination in East Timor and voiced support for a campaign for the former Portugese colony's independence from Jakarta, contrary to Australian policy.

Canberra recognises Indonesia's incorporation of the former Portugese colony but government members joined in a resolution congratulating joint Nobel Peace laureate Jose Ramos-Horta in his push for East Timorese independence.
Ramos-Horta was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize last week along with Bishop Carlos Belo of East Timor.

"The Senate calls on the Australian government to represent forcefully to the Indonesian government Australia's support for democracy and the rule of law in Indonesia," the unanimous resolution read, in part.
Opposition to Indonesia's occupation of East Timor is concentrated in the fringe of Australian politics and the resolution was sponsored by Greens senator Bob Brown.

"It is... a breakthrough in that for the first time (Australian Prime Minister John) Howard government representatives have backed a strong rebuke for the Suharto government's role in removing opposition leader Megawati Sukarnoputri from office," Brown said in a statement.
The vote is not binding on the government and a spokesman for Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer said the resolution made no difference to government policy.
Ramos-Horta, an exiled East Timorese resistance leader, was named joint winner of the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday.
Megawati was ousted from the leadership of the Indonesian Democratic Party in July by government-backed rivals.
The United Nations does not recognise Jakarta's annexation of East Timor, which Indonesia invaded in 1975.
